changes.after: while comparison and cycle changes stay below \(2.4\times10^{-14}\) kcal/mol. Here the saved comparison statistic is \(\max_i|[(H-G)Bz]_i|\), over ligand estimates, and the saved cycle-residual-change statistic is \(\max_e|[Bz-BG(Bz)]_e|\), over candidate edges: the latter is the change in the edge-fit residual after the common potential shift, not a separately normalised sum around a chosen cycle basis. The recorded values are respectively \(1.6237011735142914\times10^{-14}\) and \(2.3092638912203256\times10^{-14}\) kcal/mol. Both are absolute component maxima, with no division by ligand or edge count, no root-mean-square averaging and no relative-error normalisation. The constructed \(z\) is centred and assigned mean absolute ligand magnitude 1 kcal/mol; the incidence matrix and centred fit maps act on that energy-valued shift. The separate saved maximum entrywise discrepancy of \(GB\) and \(HB\) from \(C_0\) is dimensionless and is not the quoted energy residual. These floating-point diagnostic residuals are not a physical accuracy threshold.\footnote{Retained definition and saved values: \texttt{emmy/common\_bias\_audit.py} and \texttt{emmy/common-bias-diagnostic.json}; the script is inspected, not rerun.}
